faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium orthodontic archwire?
faq.a: Grade 23 ELI (ASTM F136) is the standard for dental implants. Better fatigue performance than CP grades and essential for osseointegration. Never substitute industrial Grade 5.

faq.q: How is a titanium orthodontic archwire manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium orthodontic archwire is manufactured using VAR melting; Closed-die hot forging; CNC swiss turning; Thread rolling. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Nitinol (ASTM F2063) for titanium orthodontic archwire?
What standards apply to titanium orthodontic archwire?
faq.a: Titanium Orthodontic Archwire components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium orthodontic archwire?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Internal hex drive tolerance +-0.02mm required for driver engagement; Surface contamination (Fe, Ni) must be <0.05% per ASTM F86. Proper material selection, manufacturing process control, and inspection mitigate these risks.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium orthodontic archwire?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
